## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 16 user-facing changes.
### New
- Sharing your screen on a page that runs in Chromium now lets you share a single tab, with its sound, as well as a window or your whole screen. - The command palette puts the best match first, ranks the pages and tabs you use most and most recently, and learns which result you choose for what you type. It fills in sites you visit, including those that start with www, and Return opens what it filled in. Before you type it lists your recent tabs, so Return takes you back to the one you were on. Start typing a provider’s name or shortcut, such as yt for YouTube or claude, to see it under the field, and press Tab to search that site or ask that assistant directly. Hold Command, Shift or Option with Return to open a result in the background, in Split View or in a Quick Window. The new Search section in Settings sets one default search for every Space and one for private windows, turns search engines, AI assistants and websites on or off with options of their own, such as hiding Google’s AI Overviews, adds your own, and chooses what the palette shows, how many of each, and in what order.
### Improved
- On Mac, tabs that use Chromium keep their back and forward history when Crest or macOS updates. - Sync settings say Up to date only when every change has reached iCloud, and Waiting to upload while some haven’t yet.
### Fixed
- On Mac, Show History now opens a hidden sidebar, as Show Archive and Show Downloads do. The History, Archive and Downloads button now sits on the page side of the sidebar, whichever side the sidebar is on, so its shortcuts open beside the sidebar instead of over it, in right-to-left languages too. - On Mac, tabs that use Chromium keep their back and forward history when you quit and reopen Crest, as WebKit tabs already did. - On Mac, quitting Crest no longer creates an empty Chromium folder in Application Support, where another Chromium browser keeps its profile. - On Mac, Crest reopens the windows that were open when you quit, instead of sometimes bringing back windows you had already closed. - Chromium is updated to 154.0.8037.97 with upstream security and compatibility fixes. - iCloud sync no longer stops on your other devices after you move a tab to another Space. A device that stopped picks up again once all your devices are on this version. - On iPhone and iPad, Sync Now and Pull from iCloud each have their own row in Sync settings, so each one responds to a tap. - iCloud sync catches up each time Crest opens. Changes made on your other devices while Crest was closed arrive, and changes waiting on this device upload, without tapping Sync Now.
---

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Crest windows on Mac no longer keep the system's WindowServer busy, which could use a lot of CPU on large or high-refresh external displays. The focused-window transparency setting has been removed.
---
Stable releases are signed, notarized, and ready for everyday use.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
